383.title: Testing
383.text:
Testing
Test strategy
See ADR 0002 for the full rationale. Three tiers, each with a
distinct role:
Unit tests (Vitest, tests/unit/) — pure functions and isolated business rules only. No DB, no
I/O.
Integration tests (Vitest, tests/integration/) — use cases and API route handlers against a
real SQLite database file, restored from a migrated template before each test. Verify post-condition
state through a read surface in order of preference: (1) the corresponding GET endpoint, (2) repo
read methods, (3) direct DB rows (last resort). Only external I/O is mocked (the mailer, push, the
SPA files).
E2E tests (Playwright, tests/e2e/) — behavior that only manifests in a browser: routing,
phase-dependent UI, modals, form interaction, mobile layout. Prefer fewer, high-confidence tests
over broad coverage.
Test quality guardrails

A test that breaks on an internal rename without a user-visible behavior change is a bad test.
Rewrite or delete it.
Never assert on call counts of internal helpers.
If making a test pass requires reaching into a private, the test is wrong.
Factories produce minimal entities; tests override only the fields they care about. If a test sets
12 fields, the factory is wrong.
No cross-test state. Each test builds what it needs.
Integration tests start no jobs loop (ADR 0011), so email and push go out only when the test sends
them: call runJobs() after a request, or deliverQueued() after calling a notify function
directly (tests/helpers/jobs.ts). Assert on the mailer only after one of them.

TDD workflow
Every code change must follow red → green → refactor. Do not skip or reorder steps.

Write a failing test that captures the expected behavior.
Run the test and confirm it actually fails (see commands below).
Implement the minimum code to make it pass.
Run the test again and confirm it is green.
Refactor if needed — do not touch the test during refactor.

Exceptions (apply conservatively):

Pure UI/layout/styling changes with no behavior change
Refactors where existing tests already fully cover the changed code

Running tests
make test                # Run unit and integration tests (Vitest)
make test-e2e            # Run E2E tests (headless)
make test-e2e-headed     # Run E2E tests (headed, for local dev)
make test-e2e-docker     # Run E2E tests against the production Docker image

Warning: E2E tests reset the test database before each run. Do not run against production data.
Tests that send real email (in make test and make test-e2e) are opt-in: they need a local
mailpit (start it with make mailpit) and the mail variables set in
.env.test.local:
# .env.test.local
MAILPIT_API_URL=http://localhost:8025
SMTP_URL=smtp://localhost:1025
SMTP_FROM='Test <mailer-test@test.example>'

When these are unset (the default on a fresh checkout), the email tests are reported as skipped;
when they are set but mailpit is unreachable, the tests fail. CI always sets them (in
.github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/ci-e2e.yml, where mailpit is started from
docker-compose.dev.yml so its image pin lives in one place) and the tests fail there if the
variables go missing, so they can never be silently skipped in CI.
E2E tests run in their own workflow so that they can be skipped for changes that cannot affect the
app — documentation, the landing page, repository prose. Adding a top-level path that the app
doesn’t use? Add it to both paths-ignore lists in .github/workflows/ci-e2e.yml.
Running another clone or workspace of this project alongside this one? See
Running Multiple Instances for the ports that have to be kept apart.
Install Playwright browsers before first use:
make install-playwright

Run a single E2E spec, or filter by test title with -g:
bun set-env.ts test bun x playwright test tests/e2e/proposals.spec.ts
bun set-env.ts test bun x playwright test tests/e2e/proposals.spec.ts:42   # single test by line
bun set-env.ts test bun x playwright test -g "creates a proposal"          # by title substring

The SPA is built with NODE_ENV=production here, as in the image. Without it, set-env.ts’s test
bundles dev React, which takes the suite almost twice as long.
The suite runs as two projects. firefox holds everything and runs in parallel; firefox-globals
holds the specs that change site-wide settings — one row every other test reads — and depends on
firefox, so it starts only once the parallel bulk is done and has the site to itself. It runs on a
single worker, so its specs don’t race each other either. settings.spec.ts is the only member
today; add a spec here (via GLOBALS_MUTATING_SPECS in playwright.config.ts) when it mutates a
singleton rather than data of its own.
The price of the dependency: a failure anywhere in firefox skips firefox-globals altogether, so
those specs report nothing until the bulk is green again. Run them on their own to see where they
stand. That also pulls in the whole project they depend on, so pass --no-deps:
bun set-env.ts test bun x playwright test tests/e2e/

396.title: Version control and pull requests
396.text:
Version control and pull requests
Commits

Use conventional commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, refactor:, etc.)
Subject line ≤ 72 chars; explain WHY in the body if not obvious
Wrap the body at 80 chars; a line with a URL, or one unbreakable word, may exceed it
make commit-check verifies the commits since origin/main (RANGE=a..b for another range); CI
runs it on pull requests. Check a draft first with
echo "<message>" | bun scripts/check-commit-messages.ts --stdin
Before committing, run make precommit
When working on a GitHub issue, add a footer: issue #123 (partial work) or fixes #123 (fully
resolves it)

Either jj or git works; the repository is git-colocated. The jj-specific gotchas an agent
keeps hitting — bracketed route paths as path arguments, non-interactive squash and split — are
in AGENTS.md.
Migration meta files conflict whenever two branches add a migration; see
Database migrations rather than resolving them by
hand.
Pull requests
Self-review before submitting is mandatory — read your own diff, check for obvious mistakes, and
make sure the PR description is accurate. Do not offload that work onto the reviewer. This is
especially important when using AI agents, which can produce plausible-looking but incorrect code.
Draft PRs are fine for sharing work-in-progress without that expectation.
Issues
Issue Type and Priority are GitHub project fields that gh issue create cannot set;
GitHub issues has the gh api graphql calls that can.

401.title: The web app (`apps/web`)
401.text:
The web app (apps/web)
apps/web is the single-page app that replaced the Next pages
(ADR 0015). It is a workspace package built with Vite, React and
TanStack Router, styled with Tailwind and the colour tokens in styles/tokens.css.
Architecture has the whole picture.
How it reaches the browser

Every root path that is not /api, /media, /locations, /sw.js, an icon or the manifest is a
page of the SPA.

server/http/web.ts applies the site password to those paths (not to /admin/**, which gets the
shell: the admin API holds the gate, and the sign-in follows from it), then serves the shell: it
reads apps/web/dist/index.html from disk on each request and answers no-store.

Hashed files are requested as /_spa/assets/…, served without the password as immutable; a
missing one is a 404, never the shell.

The router owns / (app/home-page.tsx: the event list from GET /api/v1/events and
GET /api/v1/site, or a redirect to the only event), /{slug} (an event’s schedule),
/{slug}/proposals/** (list, quick voting, new, edit; ?viewProposal= opens the modal), the

public/sw.js (registered by main.tsx outside the dev server) caches the shell and the
/_spa/assets/ files. SPA navigations go to the network first and fall back to the cached shell,
so a new build shows as soon as it is reachable; /api, /media and the other server paths are
never touched. A page compares the shell’s build id with /api/v1/health (app/reload-offer.tsx:
on load, every 5 minutes, on online and when the tab is shown). The viewer is remembered in
localStorage so the saved schedule opens offline.


The files are read relative to the working directory, so the same code serves make start, and the
Docker image, which copies apps/web/dist next to dist/server.
Build and run

make build and the E2E web server run vite build apps/web and scripts/build-server.ts (one
esbuild bundle, dist/server/main.mjs; the native addons stay external); the Dockerfile does the
same. The server serves what is in apps/web/dist, so rebuild the SPA after changing it when
testing through the server.
make dev rebuilds the bundle on change, runs it on PORT + 1 with node --watch, and runs Vite
on PORT (default 3000). Open the Vite port: it serves the SPA with hot reload and proxies
/api, /media and the other server paths to the Node server. The shell gate does not apply in
dev.

Layout and rules
apps/web/src/ holds app/ (layout, nav bar, shell, pages), ui/ (dialog, button, tooltip, icons,
notices), features/schedule/, replica/, commands/ and queries/ (the replica: store, apply
from packages/contracts/src/feed-apply.ts, feed client, sync state, a server clock offset and
IndexedDB persistence keyed by event and viewer, opened as stale). dependency-cruiser enforces
that the package imports packages/domain, packages/contracts and packages/api-client only
(never server/, utils/ or db/), that nothing imports it, that features/ never imports
api-client, and that it declares what it imports. See Architecture rules.
The admin pages are the SPA’s one lazy chunk (lazyRouteComponent over app/admin-pages.tsx in
router.tsx). The chart wrappers (ui/charts/) import @observablehq/plot dynamically, so Plot is
a third chunk, fetched when the statistics show a chart. Import admin code only from that module’s
graph, and never import admin-pages statically elsewhere, or attendees download it again.
The viewer and the user picker
Who the browser acts as comes from GET /api/v1/me/identity (ViewerProvider, app/viewer.tsx):
guestId is undefined until the server answers, then a guest id or null. The replica and the
command runner are opened for that guest, never for one read from a persisted copy. choose and
signOut call PUT/DELETE on the same path. A protected name answers guest.protected and
UserMenu sends the user to the sign-in, /auth/login?guest=<id>; a successful login reloads /.
The picker lists the guests it is given: the event snapshot’s guests (members and hosts) on an
event page, the attendee directory (GET /attendees, everyone) on /guests. Sign-out and a switch
between names clear the device’s persisted replicas (persistence.clear()); a change of guestId
also closes the feed and reopens the replica, the command runner and the queries
(useScheduleSession does: the viewer is part of its effect key). The provider asks again every 5 s
while the first identity fetch fails. commands/keys.ts holds the newKey the runner needs.
